# Best Open-Ear Earbuds for Running (October 2026)

| Pick | Price | Battery | Water rating | Best for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Shokz OpenRun Pro 2** | $125–$180 | 12 hr | IP55 | Hearing traffic, staying put |
| **Bose Ultra Open Earbuds** | ~$199 (from $299) | 7–7.5 hr | IPX4 | Sound quality, comfort |
| **Shokz OpenDots 2** | $200 | 10 hr (40 with case) | IP57 | Long runs, rain |
| **Soundcore AeroFit 2** | ~$80 | 10 hr (42 with case) | IP55 | Value |
| **JLab Flex Open** | ~$40 | 7 hr | IP55 | Trying open-ear cheaply |

### Shokz OpenRun Pro 2: best for most runners
This is a bone-conduction neckband with extra speakers for bass. It leaves your ears the most open of any style here, which matters on roads. It has physical buttons that are easy to use mid-stride, USB-C charging, and 12-hour battery life. WIRED called it the best running headphone available. Downsides: the band can conflict with ponytails, hoods, and high collars, and clarity is a bit behind the Bose.
- It's often $125 at REI and Best Buy, compared with $180 at Amazon ([WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/), [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)).

### Bose Ultra Open Earbuds: best sound
Runner's World named these best overall after more than 2,200 logged miles. They don't bounce and work well with hats and glasses. They have the cleanest sound and the least sound leakage of the clip-ons ([Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/), [RTINGS comparison](https://www.rtings.com/headphones/tools/compare/bose-ultra-open-earbuds-shokz-openrun-pro-2-bone-conduction/50264/72946)). Downsides: only IPX4, so they're not ideal in heavy rain, and battery life is about 7 hours. **Bose is expected to release a successor within about a month**, so you may want to wait or buy at the $199 sale price.

### Shokz OpenDots 2: best for marathon training
These clip-ons have the best battery life and the toughest water resistance (IP57) of the group. WIRED has submerged them without problems ([WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)). They're available at $200 from Amazon, Best Buy, or Shokz.

### Soundcore AeroFit 2: best value
This ear-hook design holds firmly while running. It has IP55 water resistance, 10-hour buds, and a 42-hour case. SoundGuys lists it at **$79.99 at Amazon** ([SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)).
- A Dealectric page offers code AFSC20 for $104 at Soundcore's store, through an affiliate link: [dealectric.com/go/soundcore-aerofit-2](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-aerofit-2). That's more than the Amazon price, and the code doesn't apply to sale items. I'd check Amazon first.

### JLab Flex Open: budget option
At about $40, this is a low-risk way to see if you like clip-ons. It's less detailed but comfortable and loud enough ([Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)).

**My take:** If you run on busy roads, get the **OpenRun Pro 2** at $125. If you care most about sound or wear earbuds all day, go with the **Bose** or **OpenDots 2**. If you're on a budget, get the **AeroFit 2** at about $80.

Note: I only had review pages in my search results, not direct product links, so the links above go to those reviews. Each one lists current retailer prices.
